His gaze lingered on a particular entry, his finger tracing the ink. "This one, for instance. It looks like there was a discrepancy in the tax assessment."

strong.text: “Indeed, they did. It was a tale of betrayal and revenge. One night, during a particularly fierce storm, Maris set a trap for Elara. She lured her into a part of the marsh where the waters were deep and dangerous. Elara never returned from that night, and many believed she had drowned. But some whispered that she had survived, that she had taken the goods and disappeared into the very heart of the marsh, never to be seen again.”

The third letter was a desperate cry for aid. Eliza had whispered rumors of a sanctuary in Greymouth, a place where Sarah might have sought solace. "If you can find it," Eliza penned, "please investigate whether these tales hold any truth. I am too frail to journey, but I entrust you with finishing our mission." Wren felt a surge of fury and resolve course through her veins. How could she have overlooked her mother's cautions for so long? She had always assumed her mother had merely relocated for a fresh start, but now she grasped the complexity and peril beneath the surface.
